stories.headline: PM Modi’s SCO visit is loaded with expectations on BRICS Summit and UNSC election
stories.title: PM Modi’s SCO visit is loaded with expectations on BRICS Summit and UNSC election
stories.summary: PM’s visit will focus on strengthening ties with Iran, Tajikistan, and other Central Asian countries; the agenda will include engagements aimed at the upcoming BRICS Summit in September, the two-year UN Security Council term of 2028-2029, and planning for the long-pending India-Central Asia Summit, which has not met since 2022
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s four-day visit to Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic is more than just an outreach to two important states in Central Asia or the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO).

The agenda will include engagements aimed at three additional multilateral platforms — the upcoming BRICS Summit in September, the two-year UN Security Council term of 2028-2029, and planning for the long-pending India-Central Asia Summit, which has not met since 2022.

Experts say the delay has led to speculation in the region that New Delhi has lost interest in the engagement, particularly compared with Mr. Modi’s first foray in 2015, when he visited all five Central Asian states.
His biggest challenge during this visit will be to reverse that perception.
In a speech given at Kazakhstan’s Nazarbayev University in Nur Sultan, addressed to the “people of Central Asia”, Mr. Modi had then promised that India would rebuild connectivity to the region.
“In an age of globalisation, Asia cannot remain fragmented.
And Central Asia cannot remain distant and disconnected from India,” he said.
Since 2012, when the previous Manmohan Singh government had launched the ‘Connect Central Asia’ policy, there had been considerable hope that more trade, travel, and pipelines would follow.
However, while trade in goods has risen from $500 million in 2010 to more than $2 billion in 2025, connectivity prospects have been considerably cut due to geopolitical shifts.

stories.headline: Congress hopes for calm in Punjab unit but storm clouds remain ahead of 2027 Assembly election
stories.title: Congress hopes for calm in Punjab unit but storm clouds remain ahead of 2027 Assembly election
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The absence of a few senior leaders, including former Chief Minister Charanjit Singh Channi, from the Punjab Congress unit’s demonstration on Friday in Chandigarh against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar has again raised questions about the party’s internal cohesion.
The July 1 revamp of the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) had sparked turmoil in the Punjab unit.

Amarinder Singh Raja Warring was retained as the PPCC chief, and Mr. Channi, the Lok Sabha member from Jalandhar and the Congress’s most prominent Dalit face in the State, was appointed to lead the election campaign committee in the run-up to the 2027 Assembly election.
Mr. Channi and a few other leaders, including Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa, Rana Gurjit and Tript Rajinder Singh Bajwa, were believed to be upset with the revamp of the party unit.
Their supporters demanded that Mr. Warring be replaced as PPCC president, exposing the factional fault lines within the State unit.

With the elections approaching and differences persisting, the central leadership of the Congress brought in Sachin Pilot to replace Bhupesh Baghel, a former Chhattisgarh Chief Minister, as the general secretary in charge of the poll-bound State.
Soon after taking charge, Mr. Pilot asserted that nearly all the leaders in Punjab have assured him of working collectively and unitedly.

Amid the ongoing power tussle, particularly between Mr. Channi and the PPCC president, the senior leaders showed a rare sign of unity by participating in the demonstration on September 9 against the Punjab government in Chandigarh, led by Mr. Pilot, a former Rajasthan Deputy Chief Minister.

A party source said earlier this week that a meeting regarding the State unit took place at the residence of national president Mallikarjun Kharge, where senior party leader Rahul Gandhi and Mr. Pilot were present.
Mr. Pilot reportedly submitted a detailed feedback report on the affairs of the Punjab unit to the party’s top leadership.
The source added, “The situation in the State unit at present is quiet, but it could be like a calm before the storm.
The party high command had asked the new in-charge to take a broad view of the PPCC’s affairs and issues and share it.

stories.headline: Arunachal Pradesh Congress Stages Dharna over Election Commission, SIR
stories.title: Arunachal Pradesh Congress Stages Dharna over Election Commission, SIR
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: ITANAGAR: The Arunachal Pradesh Congress Committee (APCC) joined the nationwide protest called by the Congress against the Election Commission on Friday, staging a peaceful dharna near Nirvachan Bhawan in Itanagar.

The party demanded the resignation and removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, a freeze on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and an independent inquiry into decisions concerning electoral rolls.
The APCC also sought criminal proceedings against Kumar and an investigation into the orders issued under his tenure.
It demanded that upcoming elections be put on hold and the electoral roll restored to the January 2025 voters' list until the completion of an independent inquiry.

The party further sought custody of all SIR-related files by the Supreme Court and repeal of the 2023 law governing the appointment of Election Commissioners, calling for new legislation with greater participation of civil society.
The Congress has cited reported differences among the three Election Commissioners over decisions and orders relating to the SIR as one of the reasons for seeking an independent review.
The Election Commission, however, maintained that differences of views were part of institutional deliberations and that its recent orders were taken unanimously.

stories.headline: Election Commission Should Firmly Present Its Side, Says Union Minister Chirag Paswan
stories.title: Election Commission Should Firmly Present Its Side, Says Union Minister Chirag Paswan
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: PATNA: Union Minister Chirag Paswan on Friday said the Election Commission must firmly present its position on questions being raised over the electoral process, stressing that public trust in elections should be maintained amid the ongoing political row over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Speaking on Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Paswan said the Election Commission, particularly the CEC, has a responsibility to address concerns raised by the Opposition.
"If such questions are being raised against the Election Commission, I believe it is also the responsibility of the Election Commission, especially the CEC, to firmly present its side.
I don't care what the opposition says because it is their job to do politics," Paswan told reporters.
"The Election Commission must maintain the trust of the people because if doubts arise in the public's mind about the electoral process itself, that would be wrong.
In such a situation, the Election Commission should firmly put forth its points so that no doubts arise in the people's minds," he added.

Meanwhile, Union Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal, speaking in Amritsar, criticised Gandhi's allegations and questioned how Congress could have won in Keralam if the Election Commission was allegedly not functioning properly.
"Rahul Gandhi has uttered all wrong facts.
If the Election Commission is not right, then how did you win in Keralam?
Rahul Gandhi is making completely false allegations," Meghwal told ANI.
BJP MP Ashok Bajpai, reacting to Gandhi's remarks, said, "Rahul Gandhi has been repeatedly rejected by people in elections.
Congress has lost its ground."

stories.headline: 2020 Delhi riots case: Supreme Court relaxes specific bail condition for about-to-be-married accused
stories.title: 2020 Delhi riots case: Supreme Court relaxes specific bail condition for about-to-be-married accused
stories.summary: Bench reduces Meeran Haider’s mandatory police station appearances from twice a week to once weekly
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (September 25, 2026) partially relaxed a select bail condition for 2020 Delhi riots accused Meeran Haider, reducing his mandatory police station appearances from twice a week to once a week.
The relief comes ahead of his scheduled wedding on October 17.
The court also exempted his appearance before the police station on his wedding day and October 24.

The short hearing before a Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar witnessed Additional Solicitor General S.V. Raju crack a “light-hearted” comment that “he [Haider] can get married at the police station”.
Senior advocate Siddharth Aggarwal, appearing for Haider, vocalised his objection to the comment made by the law officer appearing for the NCT of Delhi, the respondent in the case.
“Mr. Raju is right.
He is saying that police stations are now equipped to conduct marriages [weddings] also,” Mr. Aggarwal explained to the Bench, which did not catch the comment.
Mr. Raju downplayed his comment, explaining that it was only said in a lighter vein.
“My learned friend is serious all the time.
He should be jovial also sometimes,” he remarked.

Mr. Haider said he was facing a lot of hardship due to a bail condition requiring him to mark his attendance twice a week, on Mondays and Thursdays between 10 a.m. and noon, before the jurisdictional Delhi police station.
His counsel said the condition was affecting his attempts to get employment as these were both working days.
